metadata.title: Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
metadata.abstract_summary: An agent that cannot directly observe its true state, only noisy or partial observations, should maintain and act on a belief distribution over states rather than a single best guess - this turns a POMDP into a continuous-state MDP over beliefs, exactly solvable in principle but intractable in practice beyond small problems.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A survey and tutorial paper: gives the formal POMDP definition, derives exact value-iteration solution methods and their computational complexity, then reviews the approximate and heuristic methods of the time (QMDP, grid-based approximations, policy search) and their respective tradeoffs.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Survey paper - its evidentiary weight is the correctness of its formal derivations and the fidelity of its account of the surveyed methods, not new experimental results of its own.
- States plainly that exact POMDP solving is intractable beyond toy problems, a limitation the field spent the following two decades working around (particle filters, deep RL) rather than resolving inside this paper's own framework.
- Remains the standard tutorial reference for the POMDP formalism itself, independent of which approximate solver a given later system actually uses.
